When I heard Jake say, "You cannot live like this, baby... in hate!" I have a feeling this storyline will be major for Neytiri. She has hated the sky people all her life: they took her sister, they took her home, they took her father, and now they took her first son. So, I'm sure that means the battle with the ash tribe, who always live with hate, will test both her knowledge and emotions.

Makes these last two years of waiting worth it. Maybe this one can teach us all about how destructive hate can be.

Until we see the good humanity has done and the cruelty of the natural world of Pandora, Avatar will remain the antithesis of Princess Mononoke. That movie showed the good and evil of both sides and had nuance. So far in Avatar we’ve only seen “man bad nature good.”

@abcdefghij337 In a philosophical sense the humans were never evil per say. Just like in Princess Mononoke the humans of iron town were doing only what they believed was right for their people in order to survive. In Avatar we see a similar approach with one difference, the humans were responsible for the death of their planet and learned nothing of her loss, they approached Pandora with a predisposition of utilitarianism for the remaining humans about the planet. At the end of the day,  the last two films were two sides just doing what is best for them, for their families and friends. But now with Fire and Ash we are seeing that convolution of war which begs of us to stop and ask: "is it worth it?" Like I said, very excited to see where this goes!

Yeah... just go ahead and add the air/sky tribe of Na'vi into Avatar Movie 4 (unless they’re already going to be in Avatar Movie 3) and you'll get the complete alternate Avatar: The Last Airbender movie series. It also doesn't really help the Avatar series’ originality that the fire tribe is the evil tribe, exactly like Avatar: The Last Airbender's fire tribe. And now based on this trailer, this will pretty much be the Avatar movie 3's plot: Miles Quaritch lives and has the human side convince the Na'vi fire tribe (which has never been mentioned or explored until this movie) to side with them, since they have always been against the other tribes of Na'vi and they both want to take over the good Na'vi tribes' lands. The Na'vi tribes have a long history of being against each other because the land and water tribes are pro-goddess Eywa, while the fire tribe is anti-goddess Eywa (which never even gets mentioned or explained in any Na'vi history until Avatar Movie 3) and the fire tribe of Na'vi want Eywa's name completely removed throughout the world. Then after multiple battles against the evil humans and the fire tribe, the character Kiri and the goddess Eywa perform a giant, magical miracle together that gives the righteous Na'vi tribes a huge advantage and helps them defeat the fire tribe and the humans. After Miles Quaritch and the leader of the Na'vi fire tribe get killed off, the survivors of the fire tribe accept that Eywa is more powerful than them and surrender to her and the two righteous Na'vi tribes and the evil human survivors get sent away again. Then the surviving righteous Na'vi and the few righteous human characters live on happily until the next Avatar movie. And sadly there will most likely be one or two sad deaths among the good main characters like the previous two Avatar movies during the final battle sequence. My dad loved the first one. As the years went on, we both eagerly awaited the second movie. When it was eventually playing in cinemas, he was admitted into hospital after a routine checkup when the doctors discovered he had a blood clot. During one of my visits to him at the hospital, we were talking about the second movie as I had just seen it. I said to him "I can't wait for you to see it when it starts streaming". He replied humorously "Yeah, I just hope I live that long!". But, tragically, he didn't. He passed away in hospital a week later on Christmas Day 2022. He had been waiting years to see it only to pass away during its release.

Now, every time I watch these films, I think of him. Both he and I loved nature, and throughout my life up until the time he passed we very often talked for hours about the interconnectedness of flora and fauna; how we are all made of the same thing, and the destruction mankind brings upon it all.  Avatar was very special to him 💔💔

I am sorry for your loss. Comfort comes in many ways, and I pray that he is at peace and with our lord, dwelling in eternal life.

And for all we know, there is access to everything, which could mean in this eternal place, we can access anything (including being on a banshee, flying around the floating mountains!)

Chin up and stay strong. And watch these films in honour of the man and I will do the same x

Like, seriously, Colonel Quarish shows up again, as if he’s the only villain on all of Pandora — so believable, right? Using Colonel Quarish as the driving force of the story, along with that tribe that rejects Eywa an, is a cheap move that limits any depth. It’s a weak plot that feels more like an excuse to show effects than a well-crafted story. The narrative lacks freshness and relies solely on visual effects, neglecting a solid plot structure that truly engages. But what’s most disappointing is that it completely lost the spirit of nature that the first movie had — that feeling of how small we are compared to Earth, the urgent call to protect the green, that dystopian warning. The philosophy of love for nature, the idea that we are one with it, got lost along the way, and without that, the story loses its soul.

I remember seeing the first Avatar movie in theaters in Imax when it came out.  I rarely find it worth the extra money to see something in 3D, and have seen a few movies like that, but Avatar was THE BEST thing I've ever seen in that format.  The flying shots were breathtaking, and the bioluminescent landscapes were gorgeous.  So when the second movie came out, I really wanted to see that on the big screen too, although unfortunately I didn't see it in 3d as my husband has motion sickness issues and I didn't want to make him miserable 😅.  But even without the 3D experience, the underwater visuals were stunning.  When it comes to the plot of the movies, I would say to expect a slightly slower paced development as it really is more of a step into the world of the characters kind of experience, especially as the characters are written from a very emotional perspective as well.  If you take to the time to let everything sink in, it's a very cool, artistic experience, and definitely worth the watch - in theaters if you can catch up on the story beforehand and also afford it.
